texts.facts: This is one of the 20 oldest matters pending in this Tribunal, hence taken on priority basis. AWARD "The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner" Sanjana @ Savita @ Savitri vs Mohd Faiyaz Khan @ Mohd. Fiayaz Khan on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131528917/ 1 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the facts of the case, on 27.05.2016, concerned police official on receiving DD no. 29A reached Okhla Red Light and found in accidental condition one RTV bus no. DL-1VC-0439 and it was told to such police official people nearby that a known person of injured has taken the injured to the hospital. The bus was taken into custody and its photographs were taken. During investigation, it was found that injured Savita daughter of Harish Chand is admitted in Trauma Center, AIIMS. Further, it was informed to police official that family member of injured are taking the injured to Vaishali, U.P., in Arogya hospital. That later on, on 29.05.2016, on Trivendra Kumar Gupta gave a written complaint to the police official at Arogya Hospital Vaishali. As per such complaint, such complainant stated that he runs a jewelery shop. That on the date of accident, he alongwith his niece/Bhatiji/injured Savita Gupta were going to meet another niece at Pul Prahladpur and on their MACT No.: 4999/16 Sanjana @ Savitri (DAR) v. Faiyaz & Ors. Page No. 2 of 33 rpt way back he was driving such scooty and injured was sitting as pillion rider. At about 3.40 pm, when the reached Okhla T-point just before the red light, such injured Savita said that her hand bag fallen down. As such, such complainant/driver of scooty stopped on the side of the road after some distance and such Savita got down from the scooty to take back such purse from the road by walking. At this time, in front of such injured, such offending vehicle/RTV driver coming into a fast speed hit such injured. Further, it is claimed that after parking such scooty on the side, such complainant ran towards the injured and took out the injured from beneath such bus. The public also gathered and they made the driver/R-1 get down from the bus and in the meanwhile, someone from the public called police on phone. It is further stated that he with the help of police persons took the injured to AIIMS Trauma Center. It is further stated that as he was concerned with immediate medical treatment of the injured, such complaint could not be given earlier. It is further stated that such injured was being treated at Arogya hospital, Vaishali. 3. During investigation, in reply to notice u/s 133 MV ACT, R-2 told that on the date of accident, R-1 was driving such offending vehicle. 4. Accordingly the charge sheet u/s 279, 338 IPC filed against the R-1. Further, present DAR also filed. 5. Initially, father of injured alongwith counsel appeared. Further, driver/R-1 appeared but none for owner appeared as per record on 21.11.2016. But on the next date, 22.12.2016, owner also appeared in person. MACT No.: 4999/16 Sanjana @ Savitri (DAR) v. Faiyaz & Ors. Page No. 3 of 33 rpt Sanjana @ Savita @ Savitri vs Mohd Faiyaz Khan @ Mohd. Fiayaz Khan on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131528917/ 2 6. Further, reply and legal officer also filed by insurance company/R-3. It is further noted by my learned Predecessor vide order dated 28.02.2017, that treatment of injured is said to be continuing. 7. As per record, no reply filed by R-1 or R-2. Further, from perusal of record, it appears that R-1 &R-2 did not even contested diligently the present case and stopped appearing in the same. 8. Further, as per reply of R-3/insurance company, the accident in question took place due to sole carelessness and negligence of the claimant/injured herself. Further, liability to pay compensation by insurance company is denied. It is further stated that injured herself was moving dangerously in traffic without any lookout and was in hurry to pick her bag and therefore forgot to follow rule of the road. But it is admitted that vehicle in question was insured with R-3 subject to its terms and condition, at the relevant time of the accident. 9. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Predecessor of this Tribunal on 26.09.2017: 1. OPP. 2. Relief. Page No. 4 of 33 rpt was pleased to close interest on the Award in the present case, that order dated 09.02.2018 from the date of framing of issues i.e.. 26.09.2017 till such evidence is led. Further, it is pertinent to note that earlier on 29.11.2017 learned counsel for claimant submitted in court that injured has yet to undergo surgery of her leg and as such, insurance company may not be able to offer just compensation, unless such documents relating to surgery are provided. 11. Further, as per record vide order dated 18.02.2020, my learned Predecessor noted that no body is appearing on behalf of claimant/injured despite even imposition of cost, as such present case was dismissed in default as well as for non- prosecution and file was consigned to record room. 12. But thereafter, as per record, on 20.11.2020, an application for restoration filed by claimant side. An ultimately, vide order dated 23.02.2021 present case was restored to it original number by my learned Predecessor but it was further ordered that petitioner shall not entitled to interest from date of dismissal i.e. 18.02.2020 till evidence is led. Sanjana @ Savita @ Savitri vs Mohd Faiyaz Khan @ Mohd. Fiayaz Khan on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131528917/ 3 13. Further, as per record, ultimately, on 22.07.2022 injured, examined himself in chief as CW-1. Such CW1 tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.CW1/A. She relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills Ex. CW-1/A to Ex. CW-1/C (colly) relating to her identity and medical treatment and bills. 14. She was cross-examined partly on that day by learned counsel for insurance company, but it is pertinent to note MACT No.: 4999/16 Sanjana @ Savitri (DAR) v. Faiyaz & Ors. Page No. 5 of 33 rpt that her cross-examination was deferred as she was not feeling well due to her medical condition. As such, adjournment was granted for her cross-examination and later on, she was further cross- examined and discharged, 15. As per record, she was not cross-examined by R-1 or R-2. 16. Further, PW-2 Dr. Mohit Madan was examined as summoned witness, basically relating to future treatment and expenses. Such witness was cross-examined by learned counsel for R-3/insurance company only. 17. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 18. Further, as per record, none of the respondent led any evidence. 19. Further, as per record, a medical physical disability certificate, issued by Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya hospital, New Delhi dated 26.11.2022 noting the disability of the present injured as 22% regarding right lower limb. Further, in the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident.
texts.arguments: Including in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. Including in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Court that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 24. It may further be noted that including in the case of Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it is held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. In the present case also, driver did not enter into the MACT No.: 4999/16 Sanjana @ Savitri (DAR) v. Faiyaz & Ors. Page No. 7 of 33 rpt witness box to controvert the claim of petitioner or even to explain circumstances of accident. It was further deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of the R-1, the accident in question took place. She further denied the suggestion that such offending vehicle was not driven at high speed and there was a red light but she admitted that other vehicle already stopped at the red light but she further admitted that she such RTV did not hit any other vehicle. She further deposed that RTV was plying in the middle of the road. But she explained her purse was not in middle of the road but on the side of the road. She denied the suggestion that due to her negligence, accident in question took place. She further denied the suggestion that as she was in hurry to pick the purse from the road, she did not realize such traffic and offending vehicle coming to stop at the MACT No.: 4999/16 Sanjana @ Savitri (DAR) v. Faiyaz & Ors. Page No. 8 of 33 rpt red light. It is further argued that driver of the bus had no opportunity to contemplate such unforeseen situation developed all of a sudden on a running traffic road. As such, it is argued that at least 50% contributory negligence be assigned to the claimant. 30. On the other hand, it is argued that learned counsel for claimant that there is no question of contributory negligence. Further, despite opportunity no evidence is led by R-1/R-2 or even by R-3/insurance company to prove such defence. It is further argued that it is the duty of the bus driver to be diligent and apply brake timely. It is further argued that even in the cross-examination of the claimant/CW-1, nothing fruitful could MACT No.: 4999/16 Sanjana @ Savitri (DAR) v. Faiyaz & Ors. Page No. 9 of 33 rpt be extracted by insurance company/R-3. 31. In this case, it is not in dispute that bag of the claimant, who was pillion rider on a scooty, fell down on the road. It is further not in dispute and in fact deposed by such injured/CW-1 herself that she went back to pick her bag and traffic signal was yellow and going to be red. She further deposed that vehicle was at a very high speed. She further denied the suggestion that offending vehicle could not apply brake due to sudden stoppage of scooty. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. Fiayaz Khan on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131528917/ 6 Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 35. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the MACT No.: 4999/16 Sanjana @ Savitri (DAR) v. Faiyaz & Ors. Page No. 11 of 33 rpt following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 35.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 35.7. 42. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company that there is a vagueness in the claim that he is unable to work since the accident and no supporting documents/ witness proved in this regard. It is stated that as such, only a reasonable period for loss of income be granted, if so at all. 43. In the present case, it is claimed by the petitioner that she was earning Rs.17,000/- per month from working as Sales person with Patanjali product. 47. It is further argued by petitioner side that accordingly functional disability of at least of 22% in relation to whole body be taken in the present case, as she was working in Sales department and same do require constant standing and moving around for long hours each day. 48. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel or insurance company that there is no functional disability of 22 % in any case, in the present case. It may be noted that in the judgment of Ram Charan & Ors. Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., MAC Appeal no. 433/2013, decided on 18.10.2022 it was noted regarding rate of interest: "25 to evaluate the submission made by counsel for the applicants, it is imperative to examine the guiding principles for the grant of interest. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. 60. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is Sanjana @ Savita @ Savitri vs Mohd Faiyaz Khan @ Mohd. Faiyaz & Ors. Page No. 27 of 33 rpt persons, it is not mandatory to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case of literate persons.
